questions.scenario: A WebFlux handler calls a JDBC repository directly.
questions.question: What is the problem?
options: JDBC blocks an event-loop thread, stalling every request that thread serves
JDBC is faster, so it's better
questions.explanation: Never block an event loop; use R2DBC or move blocking work to boundedElastic deliberately.

questions.scenario: A developer writes rate.map(r -> repository.save(quote(r))) and the quote is never saved.
questions.question: Why?
options: map returns a Mono<Mono<Quote>>; the inner Mono is never subscribed. Use flatMap
questions.explanation: Use flatMap for functions that return a Mono or Flux.

questions.scenario: Rate ticks for one pair must be applied to the database strictly in order.
questions.question: Which operator fits?
questions.explanation: concatMap processes one inner publisher at a time, preserving order.

questions.scenario: A market feed produces rates faster than a mobile client on 3G can receive them.
questions.question: Which backpressure strategy suits prices?
options: Block the feed until the client catches up
onBackpressureLatest: the client gets the newest rate, never a backlog of stale ones
questions.explanation: An old price is worthless; keep only the latest.

questions.scenario: The rates service has one simulated feed that every client subscribes to, seeing only ticks after they join.
questions.question: What kind of publisher is that?
questions.explanation: A hot publisher emits regardless of subscribers; a cold one starts again for each.

questions.scenario: You need live rates in a browser: one-way, over plain HTTP, reconnecting automatically.
questions.question: What fits best?
options: A Kafka consumer in the browser
questions.explanation: SSE is simple, one-way and proxy-friendly.

questions.scenario: In Spring Boot 4, a service fails to start: no bean of type WebClient.Builder.
questions.question: What's missing?
questions.explanation: Boot 4 moved client auto-configuration into its own starters, like spring-boot-starter-restclient.

questions.scenario: A test of an SSE endpoint must check three events arrive within 10 seconds.
questions.question: What's the right tool?
options: A unit test of the controller method without subscribing
StepVerifier on the response body, with take(3) and verify(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
questions.explanation: StepVerifier subscribes and asserts signals with a timeout.
